beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A two-way table sorts the same people by two questions at once. Find a group's percent, then compare groups to see whether their answers are linked.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seventy-five students. One dot each. We ask two questions: which grade, and do you have a curfew?

do.text: The same students, sorted two ways

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: First, grade: twenty-five seventh graders and fifty eighth graders.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Then, within each grade, curfew: yes or no. Each student lands in exactly one cell.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count the dots, and we have a two-way table.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The counts across each row make its total. Twenty plus five makes twenty-five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For eighth grade, fifty altogether and twenty yes leaves thirty without a curfew.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What percent of the seventh graders have a curfew?

do.text: What percent of Grade 7 has a curfew?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The question names seventh graders. Their whole is twenty-five; twenty of them have a curfew.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Draw each row as a bar. Fifty students makes a bar twice as long as twenty-five.

do.text: What percent of Grade 7 has a curfew?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The green parts both count twenty. Same count. But do they fill the same share of their groups?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Stretch the shorter bar. Its green and orange parts stretch together.

do.text: Make the wholes the same length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each full bar is one hundred percent of its own grade. No students were added; only the drawing's scale changed.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Look at the green: eighty percent of seventh graders, but forty percent of eighth graders.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Percent means out of one hundred. Twenty out of twenty-five equals eighty out of one hundred: eighty percent.

do.text: What percent of Grade 7 has a curfew?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For eighth graders, twenty out of fifty equals forty out of one hundred: forty percent.

do.text: What percent of Grade 8 has a curfew?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Why not divide twenty by seventy-five? That uses all students as the whole.

do.text: What percent of Grade 7 has a curfew?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: About twenty-seven percent of all students are seventh graders with a curfew. That's a different question.

do.text: Of all students: in Grade 7 AND has a curfew.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For the percent within seventh grade, use twenty-five underneath. Divide the matching count by the group's total, then multiply by one hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Of adults without a dog, what percent walk daily? Eight out of twenty.

do.text: Of adults without a dog, what percent walk daily?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Stretch to equal wholes: forty percent without a dog; seventy-five percent with one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Of students playing a sport, what percent eat breakfast daily? Twelve out of thirty.

do.text: Of students playing a sport, what percent eat breakfast daily?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Stretch to equal wholes: forty percent with a sport; forty percent without. Same share.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Compare each pair. When the shares differ a lot, the two things are linked: an association.

do.text: Each full bar = 100% of its group.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: When the shares are about the same, there is no association. Here, breakfast is equally common in both groups.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Find the group the question names; its total is the whole.

do.text: Find the group the question names.
